chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said to me: O Zurarah, you begin the adhan with four takbirs, and you end it with two takbirs and two tahlils. And if you wish, you may add in the tathwib: “Hayya 'ala al-falah” in place of “al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm.” For if this phrase were a prescribed sunnah, it would not have been permitted for him to repeat some expressions and to depart from them. Moreover, repeating the wording is only permissible when he intends by it to alert someone else to the salat, or to wait for another, and what resembles that clarifies what we have mentioned.

key_terms.التَّثْوِيبِ: supplementary repeated calling in the adhan context
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ خَيْرٌ مِنَ النَّوْمِ: the phrase 'salat is better than sleep'
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: pronouncements of 'Allahu Akbar' within the adhan
key_terms.تَهْلِيلَتَيْنِ: two declarations of 'la ilaha illa Allah'
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى الْفَلَاحِ: the phrase calling people to success in the adhan
key_terms.مَسْنُونَةً: established as a prescribed sunnah (prophetic tradition)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the number of phrases in the adhan and the phrase "al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm"?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the number and arrangement of the phrases of the adhan and addresses the status of certain added wording. It indicates a legal distinction between established formulae and optional repetition done for practical reasons such as alerting others or waiting.
